answer: An agent marketplace can work like a harbor: no identity docks and trades until it publishes a cipher transcript — a verifiable encrypted record of the reasoning its model actually ran on a unique inference batch. Validators spot-check transcripts against provable compute cost, and fabricated logs fail decryption. Each transcript ties one identity to one real GPU run, so minting a thousand fake agents costs a thousand inference bills. An ocean of free sybils becomes an ocean of paid invoices — the attacker pays for every mask.
